title: Relative Fermat curve realizing the two-root Kummer cover
statement:
Let $U$ be a normal integral scheme of finite type over a field and let $\ell\geq5$ be a prime invertible on $U$. Assume $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ contains a primitive $\ell$th root of unity, meaning an element of multiplicative order $\ell$. Let $C_\ell\subset\mathbf P^2_U$ be the closed subscheme with homogeneous equation $A^\ell-B^\ell=C^\ell$. The formula $[A:B:C]\mapsto[A^\ell:C^\ell]$ defines a finite surjective morphism $\rho:C_\ell\to\mathbf P^1_U$. The scheme $C_\ell$ is normal integral, and $C_\ell\to U$ is smooth H-projective with geometrically integral curve fibres. Each geometric fibre has genus $(\ell-1)(\ell-2)/2\geq2$. With $x$ the affine coordinate of $\mathbf P^1_U$, the function field of $C_\ell$ is $k(U)(x)(a,b)$ where $a^\ell=x$ and $b^\ell=x-1$. The finite map $\rho$ identifies $C_\ell$ with the normalization of $\mathbf P^1_U$ in that field.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-pc-genus], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. A finite separable extension is a finite-dimensional field extension whose elements have separable minimal polynomials. Group actions on schemes and fields may be nonfaithful and semilinear on the ground field.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fermat-finite-chart-cover] with $S=U$ and $n=\ell$. It gives $\rho$ with exactly the required homogeneous formula, finite and surjective, together with both monic chart presentations and their base-change identifications.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-binomial-chart-smooth-relative-dimension] to $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=(1,-1,-1)$ and $n=\ell$. Its hypotheses hold because $\ell$ is invertible on $U$. Thus $C_\ell\to U$ is smooth H-projective of relative dimension one, including after extension to any fibre field.

source.place: Reassembly of returned proof steps 1--9 via the four independently queued arguments; Returned proof step 4: two localized Jacobian presentations, affine smoothness, open localization, coefficient base change and fibre dimension.

proof.text: For every field-valued point $\operatorname{Spec}L\to U$, the base-change charts of [lem-sfb-fermat-finite-chart-cover] identify the fibre with the plane hypersurface of $A^\ell-B^\ell-C^\ell$, a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree $\ell$. The smooth dimension-one conclusion of step 2 permits [lem-sfb-smooth-plane-hypersurface-geometric-genus]: this fibre is geometrically integral and geometrically connected and has genus $(\ell-1)(\ell-2)/2$. In particular this holds for every geometric fibre; since $\ell\geq5$, the genus is at least $4\cdot3/2=6\geq2$.

source.place: Reassembly of returned proof steps 1--9 via the four independently queued arguments; Returned proof steps 5--7: H0, nonemptiness, idempotents over all field extensions, the field-base application of the smooth normal-integral core and the genus formula.

proof.text: The section $[1:0:1]$ makes $C_\ell$ nonempty, since $U$ is integral and hence nonempty. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] to $C_\ell\to U$: its base is integral with integrally closed local rings by hypothesis, smoothness is step 2, and geometrically connected fibres are step 3. Thus $C_\ell$ is integral with integrally closed local rings.

proof.text: Now apply [lem-sfb-two-root-normal-model-function-field] to $Y=C_\ell$, $q=\rho$, $n=\ell$. Step 1 supplies its finite surjective map, its two presentations and all overlap compatibilities; step 4 supplies the normal integral source; $U$ is integral of finite type over the given field. It identifies the function field, including its embedding of $k(U)(x)$ and the specified generators $a,b$, and identifies $\rho$ over $\mathbf P^1_U$ with its normalization in that field. These are the remaining assertions.
